visionHint: Flag exterior and aerial photos where the horizon, waterline, or distant ground plane is tilted. Do not flag sloped terrain or hills that are genuinely inclined.
cvHint: Detect the dominant long near-horizontal edge (horizon or distant tree line) and flag tilt above 0.75 degrees. Starting value, calibrate.

visionHint: Flag ground-level exterior photos where house corners, siding seams, columns, or chimneys lean. Do not flag the natural convergence in high oblique drone photos.
cvHint: Sobel edge orientation on a 1024 px luma image: collect strong edges within 15 degrees of vertical, compute the length-weighted median deviation from vertical, and flag above 1.0 degree. Skip when fewer than 8 qualifying edges. Starting values, calibrate.

visionHint: Compare to the original and flag when automated vertical correction stretches the top of the frame, makes ceilings or roofs look top-heavy, squashes furniture, or crops away content that was in the original.
Flag photos where the manual Upright or Transform result is wrong: verticals over-corrected to lean outward, horizontals skewed, or objects stretched or tilted by the warp.

deescalateTo.when: only a small part of a minor gable is clipped and the main roofline is intact

visionHint: Flag exterior photos where the roof peak, gable apex, or ridge touches or passes the top edge of the frame. Compare with the original when available: if the original shows the peak, the crop came from editing and can be redone.

escalateTo.when: the chimney top is cut off in the primary front exterior photo (important architecture cropped off)

visionHint: Flag chimneys whose top or cap is cut off by the frame edge. Compare with the original when available to see whether the crop came from editing.

escalateTo.when: a defining feature (turret, dormer, porch columns, front entry, vaulted ceiling peak) is cut off in a primary photo

visionHint: Flag photos where cupolas, dormers, columns, arches, coffered or vaulted ceilings, or other defining details are cut off by the frame. Do not flag intentional detail crops when the full feature appears in another photo.

checklistText: Excessive cropping of ceilings or floors

escalateTo.when: crown molding, a coffered or vaulted ceiling, or a flooring feature is cut off

visionHint: Flag interior photos cropped so tightly that the ceiling line or the floor plane is lost and the room feels compressed. Do not flag photos where the ceiling and floor are simply small but present.

escalateTo.when: a main piece (bed, sofa, dining table, island) is cut by the frame edge

visionHint: Flag main furniture pieces sliced by the frame edge. Do not flag small accent pieces partially cropped at the edges.

checklistText: Incorrect framing of important property features
visionHint: Flag photos where a key feature (fireplace, island, view window, staircase, pool) is cut off, pushed into a corner, or partly out of frame. Do not flag intentional detail shots.

checklistText: Images where perspective correction unnecessarily reduces the apparent room size
visionHint: Compare to the original and flag when perspective correction cropped away walls, floor, or ceiling so the room reads smaller than in the original capture.

checklistText: Uneven architecture caused by AI corrections

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Compare to the original and flag walls, door frames, windows, or rooflines that became wavy, uneven, or misaligned after AI correction. Report the specific element; do not suggest an AI re-edit before a human reviews it.

checklistText: Composition that cuts off important parts of the home

escalateTo.when: it is the primary front exterior photo (important architecture cropped off)

visionHint: Flag exterior compositions that cut off part of the house, garage, porch, or roof at the frame edge. Do not flag intentional detail or corner shots when a full view exists.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag shots aimed into a corner with little of the room visible, or with a wall edge splitting the frame. Do not flag a two-point corner view that shows two full walls and the room's depth.

checklistText: Images with excessive ceiling or floor space

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag interiors where the ceiling or the floor takes up much more of the frame than the walls and furnishings (camera too low or too high). Do not flag rooms where a vaulted or coffered ceiling is the feature.

checklistText: Images with important features unnecessarily blocked
visionHint: Flag photos where a foreground object or a camera position blocks a key feature (island, fireplace, view, staircase). Do not flag features partly hidden by furniture in its normal functional place.

checklistText: Overly wide compositions that misrepresent the room
visionHint: Flag compositions so wide that the room looks much larger than it is, with stretched edges and tiny furniture. Do not flag normal wide-angle real estate framing.

deescalateTo.when: slightly off-center but the whole home is visible and balanced

visionHint: Flag primary front exterior photos where the home sits noticeably left or right of center or is unbalanced in the frame. Do not flag intentional two-thirds compositions that keep the whole home visible.

checklistText: Insufficient breathing room around the structure

escalateTo.when: the home touches the frame edges in the primary exterior photo

visionHint: Flag exterior photos where the house fills the frame edge to edge with no sky or ground margin. Do not flag tight detail shots of entries or features.

escalateTo.when: most of the frame is near-black with no recoverable detail (unusable photograph)

visionHint: Confirm the photo reads dark overall: crushed shadows and room details hard to see. Do not flag intentional twilight, night exteriors, or moody accent lighting in a theater room.
cvHint: Luma histogram on a 1024 px image: flag when median luma is below 70 or more than 30% of pixels are below 20 (0 to 255). Skip TWILIGHT_EXTERIOR. Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: large areas are blown to pure white with no recoverable detail (unusable photograph)

visionHint: Confirm walls, floors, or exterior surfaces are washed out with lost texture and color. Do not flag bright white rooms that keep texture and edge detail.
cvHint: Flag when more than 15% of pixels outside window bboxes have luma at or above 250, or median luma exceeds 200. Starting values, calibrate.

checklistText: Blown-out windows where useful exterior detail should be visible

deescalateTo.when: the window is small or the view is only sky

visionHint: Flag windows or glass doors that are pure white with no visible exterior (trees, sky, structures) when the view matters or the original brackets show detail. Do not flag frosted or privacy glass.
cvHint: Within window bboxes from vision, flag when more than 60% of pixels are clipped (any channel at or above 250). Starting value, calibrate.

deescalateTo.when: slightly dark but detail is readable

visionHint: Confirm the interior looks dim or dingy compared with a bright, inviting real estate standard. Do not flag intentional twilight, night exteriors, or moody accent lighting in a theater room.
cvHint: Flag interiors with median luma below 95 or mean luma of the brightest wall regions below 150 (0 to 255). Starting values, calibrate.

visionHint: Flag bright circular hotspots on walls or ceilings near the camera from direct flash, or specular flash glare on surfaces. Do not flag sunlight patches through windows.

escalateTo.when: one side of the room or the foreground is clearly blown while the rest is dark

visionHint: Flag photos where near areas are much brighter than far areas (flash falloff) or one side is lit while the other is dark. Do not flag natural window light falling across a room.

escalateTo.when: hard shadows obscure features or look like dark stains

visionHint: Flag hard-edged shadows from flash or direct sun that cut across furniture or walls, or doubled shadows from multiple flashes. Do not flag soft natural shadows that give depth.
Flag gray, low-contrast, murky shadow areas with brownish or desaturated tones typical of over-blended HDR. Do not flag dark materials such as dark wood or charcoal walls.
Flag the overcooked HDR look: flattened tones, gray whites, crunchy textures, glowing edges, and unnatural local contrast. Do not flag a clean, natural blend with open shadows.

checklistText: HDR halos around windows and architecture
visionHint: Flag bright or dark glows outlining window frames, rooflines, trees, or furniture edges caused by tone mapping. Do not flag real light spill from a window onto a wall.

escalateTo.when: bright edges outline the home or main features in a hero photo

visionHint: Flag thin bright outlines along edges (rooflines, door frames, furniture) from sharpening, masking, or tone mapping. Do not flag real highlights on glossy trim.

escalateTo.when: shadows and highlights are both clipped so detail is lost

visionHint: Confirm the image looks harsh with deep blacks and hot whites that hide detail. Do not flag twilight shots with naturally strong contrast.
cvHint: Flag when luma standard deviation exceeds 75 and more than 5% of pixels are clipped at each end (0 to 255). Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the photo is a hero image and looks gray and dull

visionHint: Confirm the image looks gray, dull, and low-contrast with weak whites. Do not flag soft, airy edits that still have clean whites and readable contrast.
cvHint: Flag when luma standard deviation is below 35 and the 99th-percentile luma is below 215. Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: fixtures bloom into large blown areas that hide the fixture design

visionHint: Flag light fixtures, lamps, or recessed cans that bloom into large blown-out blobs or cast hot circles on walls. Do not flag a normally lit fixture with a small bright core.

checklistText: Inconsistent exposure across images of the same room

escalateTo.when: the difference is obvious when the photos are viewed side by side

visionHint: Among photos of the same room, flag angles noticeably brighter or darker than the others. Name the outliers.
cvHint: Group photos by room label and visual similarity; compute mean luma per photo; flag photos more than about 0.5 EV (roughly 18% mean luma) from the room median. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Strong differences in brightness across the gallery

escalateTo.when: several photos clearly stand out as darker or brighter in the gallery grid

visionHint: Review interior photos as a grid and flag those that clearly stand out as darker or brighter than the rest. Exclude twilight and night shots.
cvHint: Interior photos only: flag photos whose mean luma deviates more than 1 EV from the gallery interior median. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Unnatural mixing of warm and cool lighting

escalateTo.when: strong orange and blue zones fight in the same room

visionHint: Confirm visible zones of orange artificial light and blue daylight on the same white surfaces. Do not flag a warm lamp glow in an otherwise neutral room.
cvHint: Split the frame into a 4 x 4 grid, compute mean b* (Lab) on mid-tone pixels per cell, and flag when max minus min exceeds 18. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: mismatched bulbs sit in the same fixture or a hero photo

reeditPromptTemplate: Make all the light bulbs in the fixtures the same warm white color temperature, keeping the fixtures unchanged. Change nothing else in the photo.
visionHint: Flag fixtures in one photo with clearly different bulb colors (bluish daylight next to warm yellow). Do not flag colored decorative lighting by design.

checklistText: Burned-out bulbs visible within otherwise illuminated fixtures
reeditPromptTemplate: Make the unlit bulb in the light fixture appear lit to match the other bulbs in the same fixture. Change nothing else in the photo.
visionHint: Flag a dark bulb or dark section in a fixture whose other bulbs are lit (vanity bars, chandeliers, pendant groups). Do not flag fixtures that are entirely off.

escalateTo.when: noise is visible at normal full-screen viewing

visionHint: Confirm grainy or blotchy color noise in shadows (under cabinets, corners, night skies). Do not flag fine texture in fabrics or stone.
cvHint: On shadow pixels (luma below 60), compute the standard deviation of the high-frequency residual (luma minus a 3 x 3 median); flag above 6. Starting value, calibrate.

visionHint: Flag window pulls where the mask spills onto frames, walls, or curtains (dark or gray halos around window edges), or the exterior view is misaligned with the opening. Do not flag natural darker exterior views that sit cleanly inside the frame.

escalateTo.when: the window view looks pasted on in a hero photo

visionHint: Flag window views that look too dark, too saturated, pasted on, or implausibly bright relative to the interior (a sky darker than the room at midday). Do not flag a balanced pull that reads natural.

escalateTo.when: glowing patches are obvious in a hero photo

visionHint: Flag surfaces that glow without a light source (bright patches on floors or walls from dodge or brush edits, glowing countertops). Do not flag real sunlight patches.

Flag virtual twilights where every window glows the same flat orange, light falls in the wrong direction, the house is lit like daytime against a dusk sky, or the ground shows no light spill. Do not flag a real twilight capture with natural mixed light.

checklistText: Twilight windows or exterior lights that appear obviously artificial
visionHint: Flag twilight window glows that are flat color fills, glow through solid walls, or ignore blinds and curtains, and exterior lights that glow where no fixture exists. Do not flag real lit windows.

deescalateTo.when: the cast is mild and only visible on white references

visionHint: Confirm white ceilings, trim, and walls read orange or amber. Use white ceilings, trim, and appliance whites as the neutral reference; do not flag rooms whose walls or finishes are genuinely that color.
cvHint: Mean Lab over likely-neutral pixels (L* 60 to 95, chroma below 25): flag when b* exceeds 14 and a* exceeds 6. Starting values, calibrate.

deescalateTo.when: the cast is mild and only visible on white references

visionHint: Confirm white ceilings, trim, and walls read yellow. Use white ceilings, trim, and appliance whites as the neutral reference; do not flag rooms whose walls or finishes are genuinely that color.
cvHint: Mean Lab over likely-neutral pixels (L* 60 to 95, chroma below 25): flag when b* exceeds 14 and a* is between -4 and 6. Starting values, calibrate.

deescalateTo.when: the cast is mild and only visible on white references

visionHint: Confirm white ceilings, trim, and walls read blue or cold. Use white ceilings, trim, and appliance whites as the neutral reference; do not flag rooms whose walls or finishes are genuinely that color.
cvHint: Mean Lab over likely-neutral pixels (L* 60 to 95, chroma below 25): flag when b* is below -6. Starting value, calibrate.

deescalateTo.when: the cast is mild and only visible on white references

visionHint: Confirm whites and neutrals carry a green or magenta tint (common under fluorescent or LED light). Use white ceilings, trim, and appliance whites as the neutral reference; do not flag rooms whose walls or finishes are genuinely that color.
cvHint: Mean Lab over likely-neutral pixels (L* 60 to 95, chroma below 25): flag when a* is below -5 (green) or above 8 (magenta). Starting values, calibrate.

deescalateTo.when: the cast is mild and only visible on white references

visionHint: Confirm daytime exteriors look orange or golden overall, including concrete, trim, and neutral siding. Do not flag deliberate golden-hour shots where the low sun and long shadows confirm the time of day.
cvHint: Mean Lab over mid-tone pixels excluding sky and vegetation masks: flag when b* exceeds 16. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Exterior white siding appearing yellow or orange

escalateTo.when: the siding reads as a different color (cream or yellow) and the original or the photographer confirms it is white

visionHint: Flag white or near-white siding and trim that reads yellow, cream, or orange. Compare with the original when available; if there is no original, report it as uncertain for photographer verification rather than asserting the siding is white.
Compare daytime exterior photos side by side and flag those noticeably warmer or cooler than the rest. Exclude twilights.
cvHint: For EXTERIOR_FRONT, EXTERIOR_REAR, and EXTERIOR_SIDE photos, mean a*, b* over mid-tones excluding sky and vegetation; flag photos more than 6 units (Euclidean on a*, b*) from the exterior median. Starting value, calibrate.

visionHint: Flag skies that are a flat, uniform, overly saturated blue with no gradient toward the horizon. Do not flag a clear natural blue sky that lightens near the horizon.
cvHint: On sky pixels (top region, HSV hue 190 to 250 degrees), flag when mean saturation exceeds 0.6 or the vertical lightness gradient from top to horizon is under 5 L* units. Starting values, calibrate.

deescalateTo.when: slightly saturated and not distracting

visionHint: Confirm lawns and trees look neon or unnaturally vivid compared with the rest of the scene. Do not flag naturally lush spring growth or flowering plants.
cvHint: On vegetation pixels (HSV hue 60 to 160 degrees), flag when mean saturation exceeds 0.55. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare photos that show the same cabinetry and flag those where it reads as a different color. Name the outliers and the direction (warmer, cooler, lighter, darker).
cvHint: Per photo, mean Lab of cabinet bboxes; flag photos whose deltaE2000 to the same-space median exceeds 5. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Kitchen island colors changing between angles

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare every kitchen photo where the island appears and flag angles where its color shifts (navy reading black, gray reading blue, wood tone shifting). Name the outliers.
cvHint: Per kitchen photo, mean Lab and chroma C* of the island bbox; flag photos whose deltaE2000 to the island median exceeds 5. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare photos of the same and connected spaces and flag where the same walls read as a different color. Use trim and ceilings as the neutral reference.
cvHint: Per photo, mean Lab of wall bboxes on mid-tones; flag photos whose deltaE2000 to the same-space median exceeds 5. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare photos that show the same continuous flooring and flag where it reads as a different tone (red, gray, orange, or washed out). Name the outliers.
cvHint: Per photo, mean Lab of floor bboxes; flag photos whose deltaE2000 to the same-flooring median exceeds 6. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Fireplace or stone colors inaccurately represented

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare stone, brick, and fireplace surrounds against the original and flag shifts in hue or saturation (gray stone turned blue or beige, red brick turned orange). Without an original, report as uncertain for photographer verification.
cvHint: In the stone or fireplace bbox compare mean Lab between edit and original; flag deltaE2000 above 8 after normalizing exposure. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Black-looking cabinets that should be dark navy or another color

escalateTo.when: the RAW comparison or the photographer confirms the cabinets are not black (materially inaccurate property color)

visionHint: Flag very dark cabinets or islands that read as pure neutral black. Report as uncertain and request RAW comparison or photographer confirmation; never assert the true color from appearance alone.
cvHint: In dark cabinet regions (L* below 25), compute mean chroma C*; flag as possibly crushed color when C* is below 3; when the original is available, original C* above 6 confirms. Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare the AutoHDR output with the original brackets and flag material colors that changed (wood floors turned orange, gray paint turned blue, white cabinets turned cream). Report the surface and the direction of the shift.

checklistText: Color changes caused by incorrect LUTs
visionHint: Compare edit and original and flag a global color grade (teal shadows, crushed or tinted blacks, faded film look) that changes material colors across the whole image.
cvHint: Compare per-channel histograms of edit and original after exposure normalization; flag when the mean a* or b* shift is consistent across all tonal bands and exceeds 5 units. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: a significant masking failure materially changes a surface color

visionHint: Flag color that spills beyond a masked area onto neighboring surfaces (green from a lawn pull on siding, blue from a sky on walls, warm glow on ceilings). Do not flag natural colored light reflecting from a bright surface.

checklistText: Blue masking leaking onto floors, counters, or walls
visionHint: Flag blue tints on floors, counters, sills, or walls next to windows, typically from a sky or window mask spilling past its edge. Do not flag real blue materials or subtle natural daylight near windows.
cvHint: Flag connected interior regions outside window and sky bboxes where b* is below -10 while the surrounding surface has b* above 0. Starting values, calibrate.

checklistText: Different editing styles across the same gallery

deescalateTo.when: minor stylistic differences only

visionHint: Review the gallery as a grid and flag photos whose overall look (contrast, warmth, saturation, window-pull style) clearly differs from the majority. Name the outliers.
cvHint: Per photo compute mean L*, a*, b*, luma standard deviation, and mean saturation; flag photos more than 2 robust z-scores (median absolute deviation) from the gallery on two or more metrics. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Unnatural skin tones when people are intentionally included

escalateTo.when: the person is the focus of an approved lifestyle shot

visionHint: Only when people are intentionally included: flag skin that looks orange, gray, green, or blotchy. Do not evaluate people who should be removed; other rules handle them.

deescalateTo.when: slightly saturated and not distracting

visionHint: Confirm colors look neon or cartoonish (wood glowing orange, grass neon, walls vivid). Do not flag genuinely bold paint or decor.
cvHint: Mean HSV saturation over pixels with V above 0.2: flag above 0.45, or when more than 8% of pixels exceed 0.9 saturation. Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: materials lose their real color (wood looks gray, brick looks brown-gray)

visionHint: Confirm the image looks washed out or near-monochrome while the room contains colored materials. Do not flag genuinely neutral white and gray interiors.
cvHint: Flag when mean HSV saturation is below 0.08 and vision reports colored materials in the room. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Severe color differences between adjacent rooms
visionHint: In photos that show two connected spaces (open plan, doorway views) and in consecutive photos of adjacent rooms, flag strong shifts in white balance or color that make shared walls or flooring look different.
cvHint: For photos tagged as adjacent (open plan or consecutive in gallery order with shared flooring), compare mean a*, b* of shared surfaces; flag differences above 6 units. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Colors that materially misrepresent the property

deescalateTo.when: the difference is noticeable but the material keeps its color family

visionHint: Compare edit and original and flag any surface whose color family changed (blue cabinets now black, gray siding now beige, oak floors now cherry). Without an original, report it as uncertain for photographer verification; never decide the true color from appearance alone.
cvHint: Per labeled surface (cabinets, walls, floors, siding, roof) compare mean Lab between edit and original after exposure normalization; flag hue-angle shifts above 20 degrees on surfaces with chroma above 8. Starting values, calibrate.

visionHint: Flag replacement skies that look like a flat stock image: uniform saturated blue, repeated cloud patterns, or no horizon falloff. Do not flag a natural clear sky.
cvHint: On sky pixels, flag mean HSV saturation above 0.6 or hue standard deviation below 4 degrees. Starting values, calibrate.

deescalateTo.when: slightly saturated and not distracting

visionHint: Confirm the sky color is unnaturally vivid (electric blue, neon sunset). Do not flag a genuinely vivid sunset that matches the light on the house.
cvHint: On sky pixels, flag mean HSV saturation above 0.65 or more than 15% of sky pixels above 0.9. Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: significant sky or architecture masking failure visible at normal viewing size

visionHint: Flag rooflines, gutters, chimneys, antennas, or treetops where the sky mask cuts into the structure, leaves a sliver of old sky, or produces jagged edges. Inspect along the roof edge at full resolution.

checklistText: House edges blending into the sky

escalateTo.when: significant sky or architecture masking failure visible at normal viewing size

visionHint: Flag light-colored rooflines, siding, or trim that dissolve into a bright sky with no defined edge. Do not flag soft edges caused only by distance or haze.

checklistText: Missing portions of chimneys or architectural structures
visionHint: Flag chimneys, vent stacks, cupolas, dormers, or roof sections that are partly erased or replaced by sky. Compare with the original when available to confirm the structure was removed by editing.
Flag bright or dark glowing outlines around trees, rooflines, or wires where the replacement sky meets the scene. Do not flag a natural backlit rim on foliage.
Flag replacement sky showing inside window panes or glass doors where an interior, a curtain, or a reflection should be. Do not flag natural reflections of the real sky that match the scene.
Flag hard cut lines, color fringes, or mismatched blur where the sky meets trees and the house. Do not flag natural depth-of-field softness in distant trees.

checklistText: Mismatched lighting between the house and sky
visionHint: Flag skies whose light direction, color temperature, or brightness contradicts the house (bright sunny sky over a flat, overcast-lit house; sun position inconsistent with shadows). Do not flag partly cloudy scenes with uneven natural light.

deescalateTo.when: slightly exaggerated but plausible

visionHint: Flag sunset or dusk skies with implausible color (neon pink, purple-green gradients) or colors that do not light the house. Do not flag a real vivid sunset captured on site.

escalateTo.when: the sky dominates the primary exterior photo or looks stormy and misrepresents the setting

visionHint: Flag stormy, heavily textured, or HDR-crunched skies that overpower the house. Do not flag pleasant scattered clouds.

checklistText: Inconsistent sky appearances across related exterior photographs

deescalateTo.when: minor differences in cloud pattern only

visionHint: Compare exterior photos from the same shoot and flag skies that switch style (clear blue in one, dramatic clouds in another, different times of day) without a real time difference.
cvHint: For exterior photos compute mean Lab of sky pixels; flag photos with deltaE2000 above 10 from the exterior median unless EXIF capture times are more than 45 minutes apart. Starting values, calibrate.

visionHint: Flag twilight conversions where the sky gradient looks pasted, daytime clouds carry dusk colors, the horizon glow sits on the wrong side of the house, or the scene still reads as daytime.

escalateTo.when: lights appear where the property has no fixture (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Flag added landscape lights, sconce glows, or window glows that float, sit where no fixture exists, have the wrong shape, or cast no light on nearby surfaces. Do not flag real fixtures that are lit.

escalateTo.when: the mismatch is obvious in a primary photo

visionHint: Flag windows, pools, or water features whose reflections do not match the new sky (old gray sky reflected under a blue replacement, or the replacement pasted into reflections with the wrong perspective).

Flag smeared, melted, repeating, or painted-looking foliage, trees with impossible shapes, or leaves morphing into the sky, usually near mask edges or removal areas. Do not flag natural dense foliage.
Compare to the original and flag any change to the roof shape, pitch, ridge, chimney, dormers, gutters, or other architectural features introduced by sky replacement or AI editing.

Compare to the original and flag removed or altered permanent outdoor items: utility poles, power lines, fences, sheds, play structures, satellite dishes, AC units, mailboxes, trees, or neighboring structures. Removal is acceptable only with documented client approval in the order.

checklistText: Unrealistic shadows or lighting caused by editing

escalateTo.when: the lighting error is obvious in a primary photo

visionHint: Flag shadows that point in different directions, missing shadows under objects, or bright and dark patches on siding or lawns that do not match the sun. Do not flag natural dappled shade from trees.
Flag fragments of removed objects: a floating cord end, half a bin, a leftover shadow or base of a removed item, the legs of a removed chair. Do not flag intact objects that were never targeted.
Flag soft, smeared, or low-detail patches on floors, walls, lawns, or counters where something was removed. Do not flag natural depth-of-field softness or plain painted walls.
cvHint: Local sharpness map: flag patches whose Laplacian variance is below 25% of the surrounding ring median over an area larger than 0.2% of the frame. Starting values, calibrate.

visionHint: Flag identical repeated patches (the same leaf cluster, floor knot, or carpet stain repeated), typical of clone or fill tools. Do not flag genuinely repeating patterns such as tile, brick, or wallpaper.
Flag smeared or brushed-looking areas on floors or walls where grain, grout lines, or baseboards lose definition. Do not flag real scuffs or worn finishes (property condition).

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Flag tile grout lines that wobble, merge, change spacing, or misalign within an otherwise regular grid, especially in removal areas. Do not flag patterned tile whose irregularity is by design.

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Flag wood floors, cabinets, or beams where the grain becomes smeared, repeats, changes direction, or plank seams disappear. Do not flag natural knots and grain variation.

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Flag cabinet doors, drawer fronts, toe kicks, or countertop edges that are bent, missing segments, or merged after editing. Do not flag real damage visible in the original (property condition).

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Compare to the original and flag door frames, casings, or thresholds that changed width, shape, or position, or lost trim.

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Compare to the original and flag window frames, grids, or sills that changed shape, count, or position, or were merged into the wall.
Flag furniture with impossible geometry after editing: warped legs, melted cushions, mismatched halves, or edges fused into the wall. Do not flag unusual designer furniture that is real.
Flag furniture missing legs, arms, cushions, or parts after an edit (a chair with three legs, a table leg erased along with a cord).
Compare to the original and flag missing columns, beams, trim, railings, built-ins, vents, outlets, or windows that existed before the edit.

escalateTo.when: an outlet or switch is missing entirely or warped in a prominent spot

visionHint: Flag outlets, switches, or cover plates that are warped, half-erased, or smeared, usually near removed cords. Do not flag outlets correctly hidden behind furniture.

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Flag shrubs, lawns, or flower beds that look generated (plastic texture, impossible plants, repeated bushes) or that were added where the original shows bare ground.

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Flag siding courses that wave or misalign, brick patterns that smear or repeat, or trim lines that break where objects were removed. Do not flag real weathering visible in the original.
Flag areas where the filled texture does not match its surroundings (carpet pile direction, lawn texture, concrete grain, or wall finish changes abruptly).
Flag visible outlines, tone steps, or color seams where an edit mask begins and ends. Do not flag real shadow lines or material transitions.
Flag color spreading beyond its object after an edit (a green lawn tint on a driveway, a wall color creeping onto trim). Do not flag natural reflected color.

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Compare to the original and flag furniture, fixtures, appliances, or architectural elements whose outline, proportions, or count changed (rounded corners squared off, a pendant changing style).

checklistText: AI edits that change doors or fixtures unintentionally

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Compare to the original and flag doors, hardware, faucets, light fixtures, or appliances that changed style, finish, or position.

checklistText: AI edits that introduce new objects

escalateTo.when: the introduced object implies a feature the property lacks (fixture, window, appliance, landscaping)

visionHint: Compare to the original and flag any object present in the edit but not the original (decor, plants, fixtures, windows, lights), except ordered virtual staging.

checklistText: AI edits that remove permanent property features
visionHint: Compare to the original and flag any removed or covered permanent element (outlets, vents, thermostats, light fixtures, radiators, built-ins, trim, stains, cracks, or damage) where the edit was meant as clutter cleanup. Concealing a property defect requires documented approval.

checklistText: Obvious inconsistencies between edited and original photographs

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Compare edit and original and list every change not explained by exposure, color, perspective, or an ordered removal. Report each change with its location.

checklistText: AI-generated details that materially misrepresent the property
visionHint: Flag AI-generated content that changes what a buyer would believe about the property (materials, condition, size, views, features). Report it as needing human review, never as fixed.

escalateTo.when: severe: the photo is unusable at normal full-screen viewing (significant blur or unusable photograph)

visionHint: Confirm whether the image is genuinely soft at full-screen viewing (edges of cabinets, trim, and text fuzzy). Do not flag intentional shallow depth of field in detail shots, or smooth featureless walls that score low on sharpness metrics.
cvHint: Variance of Laplacian on a 1024 px wide luma image: flag below 60, severe below 25. Also compute on a 3 x 3 grid; when the best cell is also low, the whole frame is soft. Calibrate per camera body and room type (dark and minimalist white rooms score lower). Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: severe: the photo is unusable at normal full-screen viewing (significant blur or unusable photograph)

visionHint: Confirm the main subject is out of focus while another plane (foreground object or background) is sharp. Do not flag intentional detail shots with selective focus.
cvHint: Laplacian variance on a 3 x 3 grid: flag when the sharpest cell is at an edge or corner while the center cells are below 40% of it, or when every cell is below 60. Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: severe: the photo is unusable at normal full-screen viewing (significant blur or unusable photograph)

visionHint: Confirm directional smearing or doubled edges across the whole frame (camera moved during exposure or brackets misaligned). Do not flag motion blur limited to one moving object.
cvHint: Ratio of horizontal to vertical gradient energy (Sobel) on strong edges: flag when the ratio exceeds 1.8 (or is below 0.55) together with Laplacian variance below 80. Doubled parallel edges indicate HDR bracket misalignment. Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: severe: the photo is unusable at normal full-screen viewing (significant blur or unusable photograph)

deescalateTo.when: only a small moving element (ceiling fan blades, a distant tree) is blurred and it is not distracting

visionHint: Flag blur limited to moving elements: spinning ceiling fans, swaying trees, moving water, people, or pets. The editor can often fix this from a single bracket. Do not flag intentional silky water in a water feature.
cvHint: Compare Laplacian variance inside vision bboxes of fans, trees, or people with the frame median; flag regions below 30% of the median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: grain is visible at normal full-screen viewing

visionHint: Confirm visible grain or color speckle across smooth areas (walls, ceilings, sky). Do not flag textured surfaces such as popcorn ceilings or stucco.
cvHint: Standard deviation of the high-frequency residual (luma minus a 3 x 3 median) across flat regions: flag above 5 (0 to 255). Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the softness is visible at full-screen viewing on a hero photo

visionHint: Confirm trim, moldings, siding lines, or roof edges look mushy while the photo is otherwise acceptable. Do not flag distant details naturally beyond the depth of field.
cvHint: Laplacian variance inside vision bboxes of trim, moldings, or rooflines: flag when below 50% of the gallery median for the same room type. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag compositions that feel accidental: tilted framing, a key element split by the frame edge, a door frame or wall dominating the foreground, or an unclear subject. Do not flag deliberate creative angles that still read well.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag room photos taken from a position that hides the room's shape or best features (shot from a doorway into a wall, from behind furniture, or facing the least attractive side). Do not flag secondary angles when a strong primary angle exists.

Flag key features (fireplace, island, view windows, staircase, built-ins) partly hidden by foreground objects or camera placement. Do not flag partial occlusion by furniture in its normal place when the feature remains readable.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag large foreground objects (chair backs, plant leaves, counter corners, railings) that occupy a big share of the frame. Do not flag a small foreground element that adds depth.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag interiors where the ceiling takes up roughly the top third or more of the frame without being a feature. Do not flag vaulted, beamed, or coffered ceilings that are selling points.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag interiors where empty floor dominates the lower part of the frame (camera too high or tilted down). Do not flag rooms where the flooring is a featured material.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag beds, sofas, dining tables, or islands cut by the frame edge in a way that looks accidental. Do not flag small side pieces trimmed at the edge.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag exterior photos where the home is pushed toward one edge with unbalanced empty space on the other side. Do not flag intentional angled compositions that keep the home whole and balanced.

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag exterior photos with no margin of sky, lawn, or side yard around the structure, so the home feels cramped. Do not flag detail shots of entries or features.

escalateTo.when: three or more near-identical angles of the same room

visionHint: For candidate pairs, judge whether the angles add new information (different wall, depth, or feature). Recommend which to keep.
cvHint: pHash (64-bit DCT) Hamming distance of 12 or less within the same room label suggests a repetitive angle (6 or less suggests a near duplicate). Starting values, calibrate.

checklistText: Images that fail to communicate room size and layout

escalateTo.when: no other photo of this room shows its size and layout

visionHint: Flag photos that show a room so tightly or from such an angle that its size, shape, and flow cannot be understood. Do not flag detail shots when a wide shot of the same room exists.
Flag bathroom compositions where the toilet is centered, in the near foreground, or the largest element. Do not flag a toilet visible at the side of a wide bathroom view.

checklistText: Photos that do not clearly show important amenities

escalateTo.when: the amenity is named in the order, listing remarks, or client instructions

visionHint: Flag photos where an amenity (pool, spa, outdoor kitchen, wine room, home theater, gym, view) is only partly visible, poorly lit, or hard to identify. Do not flag when another photo shows the amenity clearly.

checklistText: Poor presentation of outdoor entertainment spaces

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag patio, deck, pool, or outdoor-kitchen photos that crop the space, hide its size, or are shot into harsh sun. Do not flag secondary detail shots when a strong wide view exists.

escalateTo.when: a key room (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom) has no wide view

visionHint: For each room in the gallery, check whether at least one photo is a wide establishing view. List rooms shown only in tight or detail angles.

checklistText: Images that misrepresent actual room proportions
visionHint: Flag photos where the room looks much larger, deeper, or narrower than the furniture scale suggests (extreme wide angle, stretching, heavy warps). Compare with the original when available.

checklistText: Poorly chosen angles that obscure desirable property features

escalateTo.when: it is the primary or only photo of a key space (kitchen, main living area, primary bedroom, front exterior)

visionHint: Flag angles that turn away from or hide desirable features (fireplace, view windows, island, built-ins, high ceilings) when another position would show them. Do not flag a secondary angle when the feature is shown elsewhere.

checklistText: Consistent white balance across the gallery

deescalateTo.when: minor stylistic differences only

visionHint: View all photos as a grid and flag those whose whites read noticeably warmer, cooler, or tinted compared with the rest. Evaluate interiors, daytime exteriors, and twilights as separate groups.
cvHint: Per photo, mean a*, b* over near-neutral mid-tone pixels (chroma below 12); flag photos more than 5 units (Euclidean on a*, b*) from the group median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference is obvious when the photos are viewed side by side

visionHint: Compare photos of similar rooms (bedrooms with bedrooms, baths with baths) and flag those clearly darker or brighter than their peers.
cvHint: Group by room type; flag photos whose mean luma is more than about 0.5 EV from the room-type median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Final gallery sweep: across every photo showing the same cabinetry (kitchen, adjoining dining or family views, baths), flag photos where it reads as a different color. Name the outliers.
cvHint: Per photo, mean Lab of cabinet bboxes grouped by cabinet identity (room plus finish); flag deltaE2000 above 5 from the group median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Final gallery sweep: flag photos where the same walls (same room or open-plan continuation) read as a different color. Use trim and ceilings as the neutral reference.
cvHint: Per photo, mean Lab of wall bboxes grouped by room; flag deltaE2000 above 5 from the group median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Final gallery sweep: flag photos where the same continuous flooring reads as a different tone. Name the outliers.
cvHint: Per photo, mean Lab of floor bboxes grouped by flooring identity; flag deltaE2000 above 6 from the group median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Final gallery sweep: across every photo that shows the kitchen island, flag photos where its color reads differently (for example navy in some, black in others).
cvHint: Per photo, mean Lab and chroma C* of the island bbox; flag deltaE2000 above 5 from the island median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: siding, brick, roof, or trim reads as a different color family across exterior photos (materially inaccurate property color)

visionHint: Compare all daytime exterior and aerial photos and flag those where siding, brick, roof, or trim reads as a different color. Exclude twilights.
cvHint: Per exterior photo, mean Lab of facade bboxes; flag deltaE2000 above 6 from the exterior median. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: skies switch between clearly different styles across the primary exterior photos

visionHint: Compare skies across all exterior and aerial photos and flag mismatched replacement styles (different cloud sets, saturation, or time of day).
cvHint: Per exterior photo, mean Lab of sky pixels; flag deltaE2000 above 10 from the median when EXIF capture times are within 45 minutes. Starting value, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: an outlier is visibly softer at full-screen viewing

cvHint: Laplacian variance per photo normalized by its room-type median; flag photos below 50% of the gallery median for that room type. Starting value, calibrate.
Read pixel dimensions; flag photos whose long edge differs from the gallery mode by more than 2%, or falls below the delivery minimum from the hub product map (default 3000 px, starting value).

escalateTo.when: some photos are clearly below the gallery's standard (unfinished edits, rougher masking)

visionHint: View the gallery as a set and flag photos whose editing quality clearly lags the others (rougher window pulls, leftover clutter, weaker color correction). Name the outliers and the gap.

checklistText: No repeated sensor dust across images

deescalateTo.when: the remaining spot recurs in only 2 photos

visionHint: Confirm each surviving cluster member is a dust spot, not a fixture repeated across similar compositions.
cvHint: Final delivery gate: rerun the cross-image dust clustering (radius 0.01 of the long edge, 3 or more photos) on the delivery candidates after fixes; any surviving cluster blocks delivery. Starting values, calibrate.

checklistText: No unresolved corrections in some angles of the same room
visionHint: Group photos of the same room. For every issue corrected in one angle (removed object, closed door, color fix, per the fix records), check whether the other angles still show the uncorrected state, and name the leftover.

checklistText: No duplicate or near-duplicate photographs without a useful distinction

escalateTo.when: exact duplicates (pHash distance of 2 or less, or identical file hash)

visionHint: For each candidate pair, judge whether there is a useful distinction (different lighting, staging, or a vertical crop for social). Recommend which one to keep.
cvHint: pHash Hamming distance of 6 or less between two delivered photos (starting value, calibrate); 2 or less, or identical SHA-256, is an exact duplicate.

checklistText: No different editing versions mixed together
visionHint: Flag photos whose processing look clearly belongs to a different editing pass than the rest (different contrast, warmth, window-pull style, or sky). The workflow check compares AutoHDR version and model ids per photo.

checklistText: No unedited RAW photographs mixed into finished files
cvHint: Flag RAW or DNG extensions, files whose EXIF lacks the editing software tag, or files matching an original bracket (pHash distance of 4 or less to an uploaded original), or that look like an unprocessed bracket (mean luma below 80 with clipped windows). Starting values, calibrate.

escalateTo.when: the missing correction is for a CRITICAL finding or a client revision request

checklistText: No significant color mismatch between photos of the same space

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Group photos by space and flag photos where walls, floors, cabinets, or fixtures read as different colors than in the other photos of that space.
cvHint: Group by room label and visual similarity; per photo compute mean a*, b* of mid-tones; flag photos more than 5 units from the space median. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: No inconsistent use of virtual staging
visionHint: Flag a room that is virtually staged in one angle but empty or differently furnished in another, or staging styles that clash between rooms, unless the order specifies staged and empty pairs.

checklistText: No unexpectedly altered architectural features between views

escalateTo.when: the change materially misrepresents a property feature (AI edit materially misrepresenting the property)

visionHint: Compare photos of the same space from different angles and flag architectural features that disagree (window count, door style, ceiling shape, fireplace design) in a way that suggests an AI edit changed one view.

escalateTo.when: the outlier is a primary photo of a key room

visionHint: Flag photos whose camera height or lens width differs sharply from the rest (one shot from eye level when the rest are chest height, one ultra-wide among normal views). Do not flag intentional detail or aerial shots.

checklistText: Gallery appears cohesive from beginning to end

escalateTo.when: the hero image or the first 5 photos break the gallery's style or sequence

visionHint: Review the gallery in delivery order: hero exterior first, logical walk-through, no jarring style jumps. Name the specific photos that break cohesion and why.

escalateTo.when: a room named in the order or client instructions has zero photos

visionHint: Build a count of photos per RoomType from P1 labels and compare it with the listing beds and baths and with rooms named in the order or instructions. Treat low-confidence labels as unknown, not missing.
Confirm at least one photo is labeled EXTERIOR_FRONT (or TWILIGHT_EXTERIOR or AERIAL showing the front) and is suitable as the hero image: whole home visible, well lit, no blocking objects.

escalateTo.when: no front exterior photo at all (missing essential photographs)

visionHint: Count EXTERIOR_FRONT photos; starting requirement is 2 or more angles (straight-on and angled) for standard packages, calibrate per package.

checklistText: Rear exterior coverage included when applicable
visionHint: When the property type has a rear yard (not a condo or interior unit), confirm at least one EXTERIOR_REAR, YARD, or PATIO_DECK photo shows the back of the home.

escalateTo.when: zero kitchen photos

visionHint: Count distinct KITCHEN angles; starting requirement is 2 or more for packages over 20 photos and 1 or more otherwise (calibrate per package). Angles must differ meaningfully (pHash distance above 12).

escalateTo.when: no photo of any main living area

visionHint: Count LIVING and FAMILY photos; starting requirement is 2 or more angles of the main living area. Open-plan photos labeled KITCHEN or DINING that clearly show the living area also count.

escalateTo.when: fewer distinct bedrooms than the listing bed count with no instruction explaining it, or the primary bedroom is missing

visionHint: Count distinct bedrooms by clustering BEDROOM and PRIMARY_BEDROOM photos on visual similarity, and compare with listing beds. The primary bedroom must appear.

escalateTo.when: the primary bathroom is missing, or fewer distinct full baths than the listing count with no explanation

visionHint: Count distinct bathrooms by clustering BATHROOM, PRIMARY_BATHROOM, and POWDER_ROOM photos on visual similarity, and compare with listing full and half baths.

escalateTo.when: the listing or instructions mention a formal dining room and none is shown

visionHint: Confirm a DINING photo exists when the home has a dining room or dining area; an open-plan kitchen photo showing the dining table counts.

checklistText: Laundry rooms represented when requested or appropriate

escalateTo.when: the client requested the laundry room

visionHint: Confirm a LAUNDRY photo exists when requested, or when the laundry is a dedicated room rather than a closet.
When the listing or instructions mention a finished basement, confirm BASEMENT_FINISHED photos exist (2 or more angles as a starting requirement).

checklistText: Outdoor living spaces represented when applicable
visionHint: When the property has a patio, deck, porch, or pool, confirm PATIO_DECK, POOL_SPA, or YARD photos show it.

escalateTo.when: the feature is named in the client instructions

visionHint: Match feature tags from P1 (fireplace, staircase, vaulted ceiling, built-ins, view) against features named in listing remarks and instructions; list any feature not tagged in any photo.
Parse each requested feature from the client instructions and find a photo whose P1 tags or caption show it. Report unmatched requests as missing and low-confidence matches as uncertain.
Match requested specialty angles (detail shots, a view from a specific room, a vertical for social) against delivered photos using P1 tags and composition notes.

cvHint: Count delivered photos with EXIF Make 'DJI' (or another drone make listed in hub config) or a P1 label of AERIAL; flag when the order includes a drone product and the count is 0 or below the product's included quantity.

visionHint: Count photos labeled TWILIGHT_EXTERIOR (real or virtual twilight) and compare with the twilight quantity on the order.
Confirm the photos designated for staging show furniture added by virtual staging, and compare the count with the staging quantity on the order.

checklistText: Community amenities included when purchased or requested
visionHint: Count COMMUNITY_AMENITY photos (pool, clubhouse, gym, playground, trails) and compare with the order or the requested amenity list.

visionHint: Match P1 feature tags (pool, hot tub, sauna, outdoor kitchen, fire pit, pergola) against features in the listing and instructions; list features with no matching photo.

checklistText: Floor plan deliverables completed if ordered
Photography count meets the purchased package requirements

deescalateTo.when: short by 1 or 2 photos with a documented reason (small property)

cvHint: Count delivered final image files, excluding duplicates flagged by GAL_NO_DUPLICATES, and compare with the package photo count from the hub product map.

checklistText: No missing files due to editing-service processing errors
No original photographs unintentionally omitted from final delivery

escalateTo.when: the omitted original is the only photo of a room or a requested feature

checklistText: Revisit or reshoot scope completed as specified
visionHint: Match each item in the revisit or reshoot scope against new photos from that visit (EXIF date after the original shoot) using P1 room labels and tags; list unmatched items.

escalateTo.when: the flagged item is a purchased service or a client-requested feature

visionHint: When a revision note describes a photo without a filename (for example 'the kitchen shot with the open cabinet'), match it to candidate photos by room label and visible content, and propose the mapping for admin confirmation.

checklistText: Corrected versions exist for every requested revision
Original defective images not accidentally included

escalateTo.when: the defective version is the one in the client-facing gallery

cvHint: Compare the SHA-256 of each delivered file with the hashes of superseded versions; an exact match to a superseded version means the old file was delivered. Use pHash only as a fallback signal.

checklistText: New revisions actually resolve the reported issue

deescalateTo.when: the request was a minor preference rather than a major correction

visionHint: Given the revision note and the before and after pair, confirm the requested change is visibly made in the after image. Report resolved, partially resolved, or unresolved, quoting the request.

escalateTo.when: the new artifact alters a permanent feature or materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare the revised photo with the previous version and flag any new artifact (smudges, cloned texture, warped edges, partial removals, changed fixtures) that was not there before.
Compare the revised photo with the previous version and flag new lean, bowing, stretching, or warping of walls, verticals, or furniture.

checklistText: No important features lost through cropping

escalateTo.when: a roof peak, chimney, or defining feature is now cut off

visionHint: Compare the revised photo's framing with the previous version and the original, and flag any feature that is now cropped out (roof peaks, chimneys, ceiling lines, furniture).

escalateTo.when: the difference changes the perceived color family (navy to black, white to cream, gray to blue) and materially misrepresents the property

visionHint: Compare the revised color with the original and with the client's note; flag surfaces whose color still differs from the original or overshoots in the other direction. Without an original, report as uncertain for photographer verification.
cvHint: In the bbox named by the revision, compare mean Lab of revised versus original after exposure normalization; flag deltaE2000 above 6. Starting value, calibrate.

checklistText: Revised images match the rest of the gallery

escalateTo.when: the revised photo clearly stands out in the gallery grid

visionHint: View revised photos next to the rest of the gallery and flag those that now differ in exposure, white balance, saturation, or style.
cvHint: Rerun the gallery color and exposure statistics with revised photos swapped in; flag revised photos more than 2 robust z-scores from the gallery on luma, a*, b*, or saturation. Starting value, calibrate.
For each revision record, confirm every corrected file exists in storage with a matching byte size and checksum, decodes cleanly, and is attached to the delivery gallery.

escalateTo.when: the older version contains an issue the client asked to fix

cvHint: Compare each delivered file's SHA-256 and AutoHDR version id with the latest approved version for that photo; flag any mismatch.

checklistText: Final delivery reflects the latest approved versions
cvHint: For every photo, the delivered file's version id must equal the latest version with approval status APPROVED; compare SHA-256 to confirm the bytes match.

checklistText: All final image files are present

cvHint: Decode each file with sharp (failOn: 'error'); flag on exception, zero dimensions, an unsupported format, or a JPEG missing its end-of-image marker (FFD9).

After a successful decode, flag gray or green blocks or repeated rows filling the bottom of the frame (more than 5% of rows identical), solid single-color images, or strong 8 x 8 block artifacts. Starting values, calibrate.
Format must match the delivery spec in the hub product map (default JPEG, sRGB, 8-bit). Flag PNG, HEIC, TIFF, or DNG files, Adobe RGB or ProPhoto ICC profiles, and CMYK.

Compare width and height with the delivery spec from the hub product map (starting value: long edge of at least 3000 px for full resolution); flag files below the minimum or with unexpected aspect ratios (not 3:2 or 4:3 unless ordered).

Compare EXIF GPS (drone and phone files) with the listing geocode and flag distances above 300 m (starting value, calibrate); compare EXIF capture date with the shoot appointment and flag dates that are not the shoot day.

checklistText: No duplicate files with confusing names

escalateTo.when: the duplicates are client-visible in the delivery gallery

cvHint: Flag identical SHA-256 hashes stored under different filenames, and filenames that differ only by suffixes such as (1), -copy, _edited, or _final2.

checklistText: No preview images sent in place of final images
cvHint: Flag files whose long edge is below the full-resolution minimum (starting value 2000 px), whose size is under 300 KB at full dimensions, or whose name or storage path contains preview, thumb, proof, or web. Calibrate against AutoHDR output sizes.

visionHint: Confirm visible watermark text or logos overlaid on the image (often semi-transparent, centered, or tiled). Do not flag the property's own signage or a brokerage sign in the yard.
cvHint: Check the pipeline watermark flag and the AutoHDR proof or final status of each file; flag any file marked as a proof or watermarked.
For each delivered photo, confirm a full-resolution variant exists with a long edge at or above the spec minimum from the hub product map.
Compare the uploaded byte size and checksum with the source file (or the AutoHDR output Content-Length); flag mismatches and zero-byte files.

visionHint: Map each ordered photo category (interior, exterior, aerial, twilight, staged, detail) to P1 labels and confirm at least one delivered photo per category.

checklistText: Files uploaded to the correct property

escalateTo.when: a superseded version with an unresolved CRITICAL finding is selected

checklistText: Client gallery contains the expected number of files

escalateTo.when: files are missing compared with the expected count

No gallery marked complete before upload verification succeeds
No missing drone or specialty photos

checklistText: No accidental mixing of photographs from different properties
visionHint: Flag photos showing a different house, finishes, or floor plan than the rest of the gallery (different siding, cabinets, flooring, or layout that cannot belong to the same property).
cvHint: Cluster files by EXIF capture date and GPS: flag files captured on a different date than the shoot, more than 300 m from the listing, or with a camera body serial not used by the assigned photographer on that shoot (starting values, calibrate).
